open_points.subject: Operator access to instance secrets
open_points.text: “An agent works with the owner's own access to Registry's host and could read the store and the instance's configuration, service tokens included” contradicts “An instance's configuration is set on its host, readable only by the owner and the Registry process.”
open_points.question: Is an operator agent an authorized reader of Registry's instance configuration and service tokens, or must those secrets be inaccessible to it?
options: The agent is treated as the owner and may read the instance configuration
Only the human owner and Registry process may read it; the agent must not have access
Different rules apply to different operator implementations
open_points.default_guess: Treat the agent as acting with the owner's full host access and therefore able to read the configuration.

open_points.subject: Readers of customer contact data
open_points.text: “Personal data — the customer's contact data (R0-06); readable by staff only” conflicts with “every contact field it records or reads passes to the provider of the model the owner runs it on — today Anthropic for Claude Code, OpenAI for Codex.”
open_points.question: Does “readable by staff only” describe only Registry API authorization, or does it prohibit disclosure to external model providers?
options: It governs only Registry API authorization; approved model providers may receive the data
Contact data must not be sent to model providers
Model providers are treated as staff-equivalent trusted actors
open_points.default_guess: Interpret “readable by staff only” as an API authorization rule and allow the explicitly accepted disclosure to the operator's model provider.
